title: Repository Optimisation Risk Management Governance
authorityBoundary: This artefact governs optimisation risk-management planning. It does not override the Charter, Authority Model, accepted ADRs, validators, proof evidence, semantic instances, or the current-state foundation authority index.

inputArtefacts.role: source strategy for post-foundation optimisation boundaries
current routing and authority boundary for future work
current command alias and compatibility surface
USF-230 optimisation evidence and non-claim record
machine proof artifact retention and pruning policy

preservedRecordClasses.authorityRole: commit-pinned baseline evidence for the one-off dev-ready foundation baseline
preservedRecordClasses.comparisonUse: used to compare later optimisation work against the accepted baseline tag and target commit

preservedRecordClasses.authorityRole: current routing index below the constitutional layer and accepted semantic authority
preservedRecordClasses.comparisonUse: used to compare future routing and lineage classifications against the current accepted entry points

preservedRecordClasses.authorityRole: execution evidence for foundation optimisation and retained non-claims
preservedRecordClasses.comparisonUse: used to verify future optimisation does not weaken proof, validators, planted defects, evidence quality, runtime behaviour, or provider posture

preservedRecordClasses.authorityRole: policy for preserving machine proof run chain of custody while pruning superseded bulk payloads
preservedRecordClasses.comparisonUse: used to verify artifact references remain either retained or explicitly marked as pruned with auditable metadata

baselinePreservationStrategy.storageRule: Preserved records remain in their existing repository paths unless a later authorised issue defines a replacement path, archive rationale, reference update plan, and validation evidence.
baselinePreservationStrategy.authorityRule: Generated reports and retained historical lineage remain lower authority than semantic definitions, accepted ADRs, validators, runtime proof evidence, and governed source implementation.
comparisonProcess: Identify the baseline record and current-state routing record that the optimisation proposes to affect.
Classify whether the proposed change touches semantic authority, validation, proof evidence, generated reports, command compatibility, retained lineage, or artifact chain of custody.
Before applying a removal, rename, replacement, or pruning action, record the old reference, replacement reference, authority role, non-claim impact, and no-regression proof expectation.
After the future implementation change, verify the old or replacement reference is resolvable and that stale, unknown, missing, or generated-only evidence does not satisfy pass.
baselinePreservationStrategy.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must verify preserved baseline and replacement references remain resolvable and must fail closed on missing or stale evidence.

batchCategories.scope: Documentation or index edits that do not change commands, validators, proof scripts, schemas, semantic instances, runtime behaviour, or evidence artifacts.
requiredValidation: strict JSON parse for changed JSON
batchCategories.ownerReviewPoint: required when the edit changes active authority routing or deprecates a previously documented entry point

batchCategories.scope: Semantic, governance, taxonomy, vocabulary, registry, schema-planning, or authority-boundary changes.
batchCategories.ownerReviewPoint: required when the change changes meaning, lifecycle state, readiness boundary, or owner-decision policy

batchCategories.scope: Make targets, package scripts, validator commands, proof commands, CI entry points, and agent-facing command aliases.
batchCategories.ownerReviewPoint: required before removal, rename, default-goal change, or coverage reduction

batchCategories.scope: Runtime proof, machine QA, generated reports, evidence stores, artifact retention, baseline pins, and chain-of-custody records.
requiredValidation: provider mode and environment boundary review
batchCategories.ownerReviewPoint: required before pruning, moving, repinning, or promoting evidence used by an acceptance claim

batchCategories.scope: Runtime code, provider integration, infrastructure, service behaviour, UI implementation, deployment, or live-provider work.

changeBatchingPolicy.batchSizeRule: A batch should contain only one high-risk change class or multiple low-risk documentation-routing changes with the same validation and rollback path.
changeBatchingPolicy.dependencyOrderRule: Semantic authority and validator expectations must be updated before implementation, proof promotion, command removal, or readiness claims.
changeBatchingPolicy.rollbackPointRule: Each batch must identify the changed artefacts, the prior reference state, and the minimum safe rollback action before future implementation begins.
changeBatchingPolicy.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must report validation and proof results per batch rather than only at programme end.

scoringLevels.name: none
scoringLevels.meaning: No semantic, proof, validator, evidence, command, runtime, provider, or user-facing impact.
minimumValidation: changed-file parse or formatting check where applicable
scoringLevels.escalation: no owner approval required unless the issue explicitly says otherwise

scoringLevels.name: low
scoringLevels.meaning: Documentation-routing or metadata-only change with no authority, evidence, command, proof, or runtime effect.
minimumValidation: strict JSON parse for changed JSON
scoringLevels.escalation: owner review when active workflow entry points change

scoringLevels.name: moderate
scoringLevels.meaning: Governed semantics, validator expectations, proof expectations, command aliases, retained evidence references, or compatibility posture can change but runtime behaviour remains unchanged.
scoringLevels.escalation: owner approval required when the change narrows compatibility, changes active authority routing, or changes evidence used by acceptance

scoringLevels.name: high
scoringLevels.meaning: Change may remove, replace, deprecate, prune, repin, weaken, or reclassify validation, proof, evidence, command coverage, implementation behaviour, provider behaviour, environment promotion, or readiness boundaries.
scoringLevels.escalation: must remain blocked until owner approval and evidence are recorded

riskDimensions.description: Whether the change alters or appears to alter platform meaning, lifecycle state, readiness boundary, controlled values, or authority order.
Whether validators, planted defects, proof scripts, acceptance gates, or evidence quality could be weakened.
Whether retained evidence, generated reports, baseline pins, chain-of-custody records, or artifact resolvability could change.
Whether developer, AI-agent, CI, Make, package, validator, proof, or alias entry points could change.
Whether provider mode, environment, staging, production-shaped, or live-external-provider boundaries could be blurred.
Whether the prior state can be restored without losing evidence, audit history, compatibility, or validation coverage.

riskScoringModel.scoringRule: The overall risk score is the maximum applicable score across all dimensions, not an average. Any evidence deletion, validator weakening, command removal, implementation change, provider behaviour change, or readiness-boundary change is high risk unless a stronger USF authority classifies it otherwise.

requiredValidations: affected semantic and validator expectation review

escalationRules: When a change could weaken assurance, classify it high risk even if the immediate edit is small.
When a compatibility target remains referenced by AGENTS.md, CODEX.md, current-state indexes, CI, Make, package scripts, proof scripts, or docs, removal requires owner approval.
When evidence is missing, stale, unknown, generated-only, or provider-mode mismatched, the risk score cannot be reduced by inference.
When risk classification is disputed, keep the issue open and require owner decision.

requiresOwnerApproval: removing or renaming an existing command, target, package script, validator command, proof command, CI entry point, or compatibility alias
weakening or deleting validators, planted defects, proof scripts, evidence requirements, acceptance gates, or chain-of-custody metadata
moving, pruning, repinning, or replacing retained baseline evidence, proof evidence, generated reports used for review, or machine QA artifacts
changing runtime behaviour, provider behaviour, infrastructure, service contracts, UI implementation, deployment posture, environment promotion, or readiness claims
changing active authority routing in a way that makes a previously current source historical, generated, archive-only, redundant, or removable
closing or bypassing an owner-decision issue, final acceptance gate, implementation gate, staging gate, provider gate, or store-readiness gate
approvalEvidenceRequired: before and after behaviour or routing summary
explicit owner decision or accepted blocker disposition
ownerApprovalPolicy.blockedUntilApprovalRule: High-risk simplifications remain blocked until the approval evidence is recorded. An agent must not infer approval from silence, issue existence, generated reports, or passing validation alone.
ownerApprovalPolicy.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must link high-risk changes to approval records before merge or Linear completion.

stages.meaning: The target or tool is current and may be referenced by docs, agents, CI, proof, or users.
The historical or compatibility entry point remains supported while users and agents migrate to the current entry point.
exitCriteria: all active references updated or intentionally retained

stages.meaning: The entry point is no longer preferred but remains available because active references, proof coverage, or owner approval prerequisites are not complete.
exitCriteria: no active references remain unless explicitly approved
owner approval is recorded for removal

stages.meaning: The entry point may be removed only by a later authorised implementation issue.
The entry point has been removed by authorised implementation and the removal is reflected in docs, command indexes, CI, proof expectations, and Linear acceptance evidence.

warningRequirements: Human-facing docs must identify the preferred current entry point before removal is proposed.
Agent-facing instructions must preserve compatibility wording until replacement is separately authorised and validated.
Future command-output warnings may be added only by an authorised implementation issue and must not weaken proof behaviour.
deprecationPolicy.compatibilityWindow: No fixed calendar removal window is authorised. A superseded command, target, package script, proof command, validator command, or CI entry point remains in the compatibility window until replacement authority, reference updates, no-regression proof, rollback path, and owner approval are all recorded.
validationBeforeRemoval: reference audit across docs, agent directives, Make targets, package scripts, CI workflows, proof scripts, validators, current-state indexes, and evidence records
no-regression proof against the affected assurance class
strict parse for changed JSON artefacts
deprecationPolicy.rollbackRule: Removal must be reversible by restoring the prior entry point or alias without changing semantics, weakening validators, or losing evidence history.
deprecationPolicy.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must run no-regression checks before deprecating or removing targets.

minimumRequirementsBeforeClosure: replacement output and coverage are validated as intended
docs, agent directives, CI, Make, package scripts, proof scripts, validators, indexes, and evidence references are audited
active references are updated or explicitly retained with rationale
owner decision is recorded for high-risk removal
referenceUpdateRules: Prefer current-state aliases in new human-facing instructions.
Retain historical command names as explicit compatibility aliases while referenced by governance, proof, CI, or agent directives.
Do not treat an alias as removable merely because a preferred alias exists.
Update current-state command surface and authority routing before any future removal.
Preserve generated-report and evidence non-claims when changing references.
ownerDecisionTriggers: shortening or ending a compatibility window
removing a command that appears in AGENTS.md, CODEX.md, current-state indexes, proof scripts, CI, Make, package scripts, or evidence records
changing a command from compatibility alias to retired
changing proof, validation, or evidence coverage attached to a command
compatibilityWindowPolicy.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must verify aliases and replacement commands produce intended outputs before compatibility can be narrowed.
